questions.text: What is the test shell register map (offset, width, reset value and access of every shell register)?
questions.default: Byte offsets 0x100 to 0x124 as listed in registers.map, 32-bit each, SH_RX_BYTE with the byte in bits 7:0 and the last flag in bit 8.
questions.reason: The request names these registers but gives no offsets, so the map is a proposal.
questions.answer:
IN: offset 0x00, WO, reset 0: [7:0] packet byte, [8] end flag
STAT: offset 0x09, RO, reset 0: [0] telemetry on, [1] busy
RIDX: offset 0x03, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
RWORD: offset 0x04, RO, reset 0: bytes 4i..4i+3 of the reply, first byte on top, zero past the end
RLEN: offset 0x02, RO, reset 0: length in bytes of the latest reply, 0 if none
TICK: offset 0x01, WO, reset 0: [7:0] n ticks
TIDX: offset 0x06, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
TWORD: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: same for the telemetry frame
TAKE: offset 0x08, WO, reset 0: any write takes the held telemetry frame
TLEN: offset 0x05, RO, reset 0: length of the held telemetry frame, 0 if none
shell: test shell, PROTOCOL.md 1.1
unmapped: no register at an offset: reads 0, writes ignored (read-only registers behave the same on write)
questions.evidence: IN: offset 0x00, WO, reset 0: [7:0] packet byte, [8] end flag

questions.text: Which counter takes a refused sequence number, repeated or out-of-order?
questions.default: Equal to the last accepted number is repeated, any other refused number is out-of-order.
questions.reason: The request does not define the boundary.
questions.answer: Equal to the last accepted number is repeated, any other refused number is out-of-order.

questions.text: Does a successful write, telemetry start, stop or status command count as carried out?
questions.default: Yes, any reply with status 0 counts as one command carried out.
questions.reason: The request says commands carried out without defining it.
questions.answer: Yes, any reply with status 0 counts as one command carried out.

questions.text: Is the status reply payload 16 or 17 bytes?
questions.default: 17 bytes: seven 16-bit counters, a 16-bit frame count and 1 telemetry byte.
questions.reason: The request says sixteen bytes and one more, which is 17.
questions.answer: 17 bytes. The STATUS payload is seven 16-bit counters (14 bytes), a 16-bit telemetry frame count (2 bytes) and a TLM_ON byte (1 byte), which totals 17. The spec does not state the total byte count directly, so this follows from the listed field widths.
questions.evidence: STATUS: seven 16-bit counters, telemetry frame count (16 bit), TLM_ON byte, all before this command is counted.

questions.text: What are the values of TIMEOUT_CYCLES and BUILD_STAMP?
questions.reason: They are supplied by the shell and not given in the request.
questions.answer: TIMEOUT_CYCLES is 100000. BUILD_STAMP is not specified. The proposed default of 1000000 for TIMEOUT_CYCLES contradicts the specification and is not used.
